answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation.. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. Consider a vine as the anchor of the cost. A nadir stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a karst...
